rows.label: Annual number of children with SAM who might benefit
Reduction in mortality rate if the intervention is successful
rows.explainer:
CHAIN's trial proposal describes sample size calculations. They assume an absolute reduction of 3.7 pp.

"If F35 treatment would reduce absolute risk of 14-day mortality by 3.7%, i.e., a relative rate reduction of 26.5% compared to standard of care, with planned interim analyses as detailed above, the estimated average sample size would be 1211 for a power of 73.4%, where 39% of trials would require less than 750 patients and 53.4% of trials would require less than 1000."

CHAIN, Reduced calorie feeds in the early management of ill severely malnourished children: A randomized phase III clinical trial (unpublished)

Funding accelerates this research by x years
rows.explainer:
GiveWell guess
This assumes that another similar trial would occur 3 years later, without our involvement. This is just a guess, but it seems reasonable based on the high importance of the question and the typical pace of progress in global health research.

rows.label: Adjustment for incomplete adoption of WHO guidance
Probability someone else would provide this funding if GiveWell didn't
rows.explainer:
GiveWell guess based on our assessment that this is an important research question and other funders seem eager to fund it.

Our calculations implicitly assume that another funder's counterfactual cost-effectiveness is 0, which is unlikely to be true. However, we have not bothered to account for that inaccuracy since it would almost certainly raise cost-effectiveness, which is already above our bar for funding.

rows.label: Total adjustment
Deaths averted by funding trial, after adjustments
Moral weight of averting a death due to malnutrition
rows.explainer:
GiveWell's moral weight, 118 units of value, times your multiplier on the value of a life.

This value is taken from our 2024 investigation into Taimaka's malnutrition treatment program and is based on the proportion of children at different ages admitted for treatment in that program. Age group proportions could be slightly different in programs affected by this trial, which could have a minor impact on overall cost-effectiveness.
(See https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1O6V1IUGmZhSfVM0y215uJkB-_CT7pUsa9CSIdGL3fK8/edit?gid=1362437801#gid=1362437801&range=B9)

Also see https://www.givewell.org/how-we-work/our-criteria/cost-effectiveness/moral-weights for an explanation of GiveWell's moral weights.
